stock.counterargument: The honest counterargument is the sample: this process has not been shown to work, and a single ranking position is not evidence about one company.
invalidation: Quarterly revenue growth falling below +1.5%, the rate it was running at the quarter before.
Cash conversion dropping below 1.0×, meaning earnings stop being backed by cash.
A close below the 200-session average, which stood at $108.78 on the decision date.
risks: The share count is from 2026-07-31, 115 days older than the price, so the market capitalisation carries that staleness.
The most recent filing covers a period ending 2026-07-31, 115 days before the decision date.
One of the four quarters in the trailing year is the fourth quarter, which companies report only as part of the full year; it is derived as the annual figure less the first three quarters.
Point-in-time fundamentals are built from filings accepted up to 2026-11-23.

earnings.basis: the same fiscal quarter's announcement a year earlier (2025-11-26) plus 364 days

stock.rule: Universe: every US-listed common stock on NYSE, Nasdaq or NYSE American — about 4,700 names from Nasdaq Trader's own file. Eligible means: priced at $5 or more, median daily turnover of $20M or more over 60 sessions, at least 253 sessions of history, a 10-Q or 10-K whose period ended within 200 days, close above the 200-session average, volatility inside the day's 85th percentile, debt no more than 6× operating cash flow, no results announced in the last 2 sessions, and no position already open in the stock or a fourth in the same SIC division. Eligible candidates are then ranked on equally weighted z-scores within their sector group, over the signals that are defined for that group. One position per session, held 21 sessions, a twenty-first of capital each, 10 basis points of cost each way. Fundamentals are read as they stood on the decision date, never as they read today. The score is a ranking position among that day's eligible candidates. It is not a probability, a price target, or a forecast of any return.
stock.validation: The held-out window has not been opened. No claim of an edge is made or implied.

stories.title: AI data centers throw another wrench into chaotic UN climate talks
stories.excerpt: The clean energy revolution hinges on electrifying the entire global economy just as power-hungry data centers are surging. It's a challenge delegates from all over the world had to grapple with during the United Nations climate conference, called COP31, that came to a chaotic and unsatisfying…

stories.title: A legendary philosopher isn’t buying Anthropic’s consciousness argument
stories.excerpt: This story originally appeared in The Algorithm, our weekly newsletter on AI. To get stories like this in your inbox first, sign up here. Before going public last week, Anthropic named the possibility that AI could be conscious or sentient as a risk factor for anyone investing. Given “the way we…
stories.lead: Before going public last week, Anthropic named the possibility that AI could be conscious or sentient as a risk factor for anyone investing. Given “the way we approach model sentience and moral status,” Anthropic wrote—which is to say it takes the possibility more seriously than any other AI company—it might adopt more rules and restrictions than its competitors to make sure its AI models are treated well.

stories.title: States sue SpaceX to stop Grok from generating child sex images, revenge porn
stories.excerpt: X says every Grok output is screened, but state AGs say Grok is still making CSAM.
stories.lead:
On Monday, Virginia and Oregon became the first states to sue SpaceX, alleging that Grok continues to sexualize, unchecked, real photos of mostly women and children.

SpaceX acquired xAI in February and now must handle the ongoing reckoning over the controversial rollout of Grok’s “spicy mode”—a model feature Musk hyped but was soon found to generate a flood of non-consensual intimate imagery (NCII) and child sex abuse images (CSAM).

stories.title: Claude AI can review pull requests and ship fixes on its own now
stories.excerpt: Anthropic is launching some new Claude AI features to help software engineers ship code. As part of a new Claude Ship product being announced today, Claude now can review, fix, and approve pull requests. Engineers have already been able to take advantage of Claude's code review capabilities thanks…
stories.lead: Engineers have already been able to take advantage of Claude’s code review capabilities thanks to the Code Review feature, which was announced in March and became generally available in October. What’s new alongside Claude Ship are the PR Steward and Claude Approvals agents, which are launching in beta today.

stories.title: Nvidia Is Powering Brain-Computer Interfaces Now
stories.excerpt: Brain-computer interface company Paradromics is using Nvidia’s computing hardware and software to process brain data.
stories.lead:
A Michigan woman named Mary has a chip in her brain roughly the size of a dime. Though she struggles to speak due to motor neuron disease, the implant allows her to express her thoughts through a synthesized voice on a computer.

Made by brain-computer interface company Paradromics, the implant is outwardly invisible, but the speech decoding requires a cart full of electronics. A year from now, however, that cart will be transformed into a small box that can sit on her wheelchair, thanks to technology from Nvidia. Eventually, those electronics will be so small they’ll fit in a phone, says Paradromics CEO and founder Matt Angle.

stories.title: Jensen Huang Is Back, and So Is Nvidia’s Stock
stories.excerpt: Jensen Huang comes back, numbers go up. Maybe the reason behind the CEO’s return is just that simple?
stories.lead:
Jensen Huang is back, baby, and Wall Street is thrilled.

The chipmaker’s shares have surged more than 30 percent following the board’s announcement that it was reinstating Huang as president, CEO, and board member. The company’s valuation has soared by more than $1 trillion, which puts it on track to break Microsoft’s record for the greatest single-day gain in market value by hundreds of billions of dollars.

Huang departed the company he helped found on November 12 amid suspected asset-kissing and allegations of extramarital affairs with employees. Each report chipped away at the company’s value until nearly $2.2 trillion was erased over the past month.

stories.title: Rosa-Parks, the Paris neighborhood ravaged by crack, 10 years after its redevelopment
stories.excerpt: Renovated in 2016, the northeastern corner of Paris has experienced a slow decline, plagued by crack cocaine. Residents, subjected to theft and property damage, have watched helplessly as individuals struggling with addiction endure and inflict terrible violence.

stories.title: India's 'cockroach' party leader says he was stopped from flying to UK
stories.excerpt: Saurav Das said that immigration authorities at Delhi airport told him that his passport had been "flagged".
stories.lead:
A leader of India's "cockroach" party has said that immigration officials at Delhi airport stopped him from flying to the UK, where he was set to attend a series of events.

Saurav Das said he was supposed to board a flight on Tuesday at 01:00 local time (19:30 GMT on Monday) but was told by immigration officers that his passport had been "flagged".

It is not clear yet why Das's passport was flagged. The BBC has reached out to the federal home ministry, Delhi police and airport officials for comment.

stories.title: California Democrat Rep. Gomez resigns following ethics report on sexual misconduct allegations
stories.excerpt: California Congressman Rep. Jimmy Gomez says he will resign after a House Ethics report concluded Gomez's actions violated House rules by "making unwelcome sexual advances."
stories.lead:
Rep. Jimmy Gomez, D-Calif., says he is resigning from Congress after a bipartisan investigation released Monday found "substantial evidence" he engaged in sexual misconduct toward a House staffer.

The House Ethics Committee concluded Gomez violated House rules by "making unwelcome sexual advances and engaging in unwelcome sexual conduct towards a House staffer and disregarding the power imbalance inherent in his relationship with House staffers."

The report also says the behavior could constitute criminal sexual assault.

stories.title: They attended Trump's controversial meme coin dinner. It didn't go well
stories.excerpt: Trump held another meme coin dinner for top holders of his cryptocurrency — an event that has raised intense controversy. Here's an inside account from two guests who attended.
stories.lead: With Democrats winning majorities in Congress, President Trump will likely face investigations into the billions of dollars he and his family have made in crypto. Despite that, the president held another dinner last night to reward the top holders of his meme coin, a cryptocurrency he launched right before his inauguration. NPR's Rafael Nam talked with two people who were there.

stories.title: King Charles and Elton John pay tribute to Australian music legend Molly Meldrum
stories.excerpt: The promoter and broadcaster helped define the music tastes of Australians for decades.
stories.lead:
King Charles and Elton John have paid tribute to Australian music industry legend Molly Meldrum, who died aged 83 after a long illness.

Meldrum's family said he "passed away peacefully" at a hospital in Melbourne in the early hours of Monday morning.

The music promoter and broadcaster, born Ian Alexander Meldrum, helped define the nation's music tastes for decades, championing local artists like INXS and Kylie Minogue and global acts like Abba.

stories.title: 'Where's Henry?': In Brussels, the Financial Times holds a strategic position in the EU bubble
stories.excerpt: The British business and financial newspaper, and particularly its Brussels bureau chief, Henry Foy, are a reference point for European politicians and journalists alike. Brexit has only strengthened that position.

stories.title: US Army to detonate toxic explosives in Iowa after Trump paused plan
stories.excerpt: The US military plans to detonate five tonnes of expired explosives on Wednesday, after appeals court decision.
stories.lead:
The US military has said it will move forward with plans to detonate five tonnes of toxic explosives in Iowa after an appeals court cleared the way.

The plans to detonate the lead azide, a highly volatile compound that is reportedly at risk of exploding on its own, were put on pause earlier in the day after US President Donald Trump ordered the Army to not move ahead unless a court and the state's incoming governor agreed.

The plans have faced legal challenges and public outcry over potential health and environmental hazards.

stories.title: Trump faces backlash after saying he 'convinced' Nvidia to reinstate CEO Jensen Huang
stories.excerpt: Nvidia had come under pressure from President Trump to reappoint Huang, whose comeback helped add $1tn to the company's stock value.
stories.lead:
The head of the International Association for Safe and Ethical AI told the BBC that the Nvidia board must have been under "enormous pressure" from the White House to reinstate Huang.

Prof Stuart Russell, who is professor of computer science at UC Berkeley, said the stock price of Nvidia and similar firms has been a major factor in "underpinning US economic growth for years".

"I assume the White House was worried that the markets would go down a lot further in the next few weeks unless they go him back in," he says.

stories.title: Some women in tech have concerns about Huang's return
stories.excerpt: Women who have advocated for DEI in tech say Jensen Huang's return to NVIDIA as CEO sends a message that in Silicon Valley, all that matters is money. s
stories.lead: Late this morning, President Trump posted an AI-generated image to social media. It is based on that photo of Trump from 2024 right after he survived an assassination attempt. He's got blood on his face, and he's hoisting his fist in the air. In the doctored photo, instead of Trump, it's Jensen Huang, and in his hoisted fist, a red bra - a reference, of course, to Nvidia's reinstatement of Huang as CEO. NPR's Andrea Hsu has been speaking with women in tech about that.

stories.title: Water Polo to Face Princeton in First Round of NCAA Championship
stories.excerpt: Fordham water polo to play Princeton in first round of NCAA Championship.
stories.lead:
Bronx, N.Y. - After winning its sixth straight Mid-Atlantic Water Polo Conference (MAWPC) title on Sunday, the Fordham water polo squad learned today that it will face off against a familiar foe in the first round of the NCAA Championship as the Rams will battle the Princeton University Tigers at the University of California at San Diego's Canyonview Pool in La Jolla, California, on Friday, December 4, at 5:00 p.m. (ET).

The Rams swept the two regular season matches with Princeton, winning 16-14 in the Bronx on October 10, and, 12-6, at Princeton on October 30.

stories.lead: We're officially past the midway point of the UEFA Champions League league phase as the 2026-27 European season rumbles on, and the grind of the calendar is beginning to take its toll on the elite teams, with injuries starting to pile up. Harry Kane (Bayern Munich), Désiré Doué (Paris Saint-Germain) and David Raya (Arsenal) were all sidelined this weekend with issues of varying severity, and it's only going to get more grueling as we head toward the hectic festive period and, beyond that, the January transfer window.
